# Sample trace: draft-papon-lake-pq-edhoc §3.2

Initiator signs; Responder authenticates with a KEM *and* a signature.
Generated by `generate_pq_test_vectors` in `lib/src/lib.rs`; regenerate with
`cargo test -p lakers --no-default-features --features \
"lakers-crypto/rustcrypto, test-ead-none, lakers/pq, lakers-shared/pq_buffers" \
-- --ignored generate_pq_test_vectors`.

## What this is, and what it is not

This is a **sample trace**, not a reproducible test vector in the sense of RFC 9529.
ML-DSA signing is randomised (hedged), so `SIGNATURE_2` and `SIGNATURE_3` differ on
every run even with every key and the ephemeral KEM pair held fixed -- and with them
`CIPHERTEXT_2`, `TH_3`, `TH_4`, `PRK_out` and everything exported from it.

A verifier can therefore *check* this trace end to end -- every signature verifies,
every hash and KDF step recomputes -- but cannot *regenerate* its bytes. Producing
byte-reproducible vectors would need the draft to mandate deterministic ML-DSA
signing. This is worth explicit text in the draft; see D15 in
`pq_edhoc_section3.md`.
